sources.text:
Riverside Substation Fire

A fire broke out at the Riverside Substation on 4 March 2025 and the power outage began at 02:10 that morning.

Dana Whitfield is the incident commander for the response.

Utility control room count: 12,000 customers are without power.

Actions so far: crews isolated the damaged transformer; the fire brigade extinguished the blaze; mobile generators were deployed to the hospital.

City Emergency Bulletin

The city emergency office reports that 15,000 customers are without power after the Riverside fire.

Residents should avoid the Riverside industrial area while crews work.

sources.text:
Hydrology Report

The Calder River flooded the lower valley. The gauge at Millbridge recorded a peak level of 7.2 metres.

The river had been rising since 10 June 2025.

Operations Situation Report

The evacuation order was issued on 11 June 2025 and 340 households were evacuated from the valley.

Emergency shelters opened: Millbridge Community Hall and Northside High School Gym.

A second gauge reading from the operations team put the peak level at 6.8 metres.

sources.text:
Transport Agency Notice

The Harlow Bridge collapsed on 19 August 2025 during the evening rush.

The estimated repair cost is $4,750,000 according to the agency.

Traffic on the corridor has fallen by 38 percent since the closure.

Rescue Coordination Log

Rescue measures so far: divers searched the river; a crane lifted the first vehicles; paramedics set up a triage tent.

The county engineer's office put the repair cost at $6,200,000 in its own assessment.

sources.text:
Forestry Service Update

The Cedar Ridge Fire started on 2 September 2025 near the northern trailhead.

Suppression costs so far total $2,300,000.

The fire is 60 percent contained.

County Situation Report

Evacuation centres are open at Pine Valley Elementary and the Lakeside Recreation Hall.

The county mapping team measured the burned area at 8,400 hectares.

The forestry aerial survey measured the burned area at 9,100 hectares.

14 structures have been destroyed according to the damage assessment team.

sources.text:
Weekly operations review, week 37

Emergency department: the median wait time from triage to first assessment was 47 minutes.

Day surgery unit: patients waited a median of 95 minutes between admission and theatre.

Outpatient clinic: the median wait time in the waiting room was 22 minutes.

Staffing remained stable across all units; two agency nurses covered the night shifts.

Radiology reported scanner downtime of 6 hours on Tuesday; no wait time data was collected for the unit this week.

The cafeteria refurbishment will finish in November.

sources.text:
Spring variety trial 2026, Northfield station

Wheat plots yielded 6.8 tonnes per hectare on average, with grain protein at 12.1%.

Barley averaged 5.2 tonnes per hectare; lodging affected 8% of plots.

Oilseed rape produced 3.4 tonnes per hectare despite pigeon damage in the north block.

Maize was sown late and will only be harvested in October, so no yield figure is available yet.

Fertiliser costs rose 14% year on year.

sources.text:
Quarterly groundwater quality report, Q3 2026

Prepared by the municipal water authority for the regional council.

Sampling followed the national protocol; all twelve wells were sampled twice in the quarter.

1. Phosphate monitoring

Across the twelve monitoring wells, the mean reading this quarter was 0.4 mg/L, within the permitted range.

Field blanks and duplicates met the quality control criteria.

2. Nitrate monitoring

Across the twelve monitoring wells, the mean reading this quarter was 38 mg/L, within the permitted range.

Field blanks and duplicates met the quality control criteria.

3. Lead monitoring

Across the twelve monitoring wells, the mean reading this quarter was 3.1 µg/L, within the permitted range.

Field blanks and duplicates met the quality control criteria.

4. Chloride monitoring

Across the twelve monitoring wells, the mean reading this quarter was 112 mg/L, within the permitted range.

Field blanks and duplicates met the quality control criteria.

5. Sulphate monitoring

Across the twelve monitoring wells, the mean reading this quarter was 64 mg/L, within the permitted range.

Field blanks and duplicates met the quality control criteria.

6. Fluoride monitoring

Across the twelve monitoring wells, the mean reading this quarter was 0.9 mg/L, within the permitted range.

Field blanks and duplicates met the quality control criteria.

7. Iron monitoring

Across the twelve monitoring wells, the mean reading this quarter was 0.2 mg/L, within the permitted range.

Field blanks and duplicates met the quality control criteria.

8. Manganese monitoring

Across the twelve monitoring wells, the mean reading this quarter was 41 µg/L, within the permitted range.

Field blanks and duplicates met the quality control criteria.

Arsenic was not analysed this quarter because the laboratory contract was being renewed.

The next report is due in January.
